issues.span:
In the virtue of all sentient beings
That brings rest from the suffering of the lower realms
issues.evidence: Tibetan སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན་གྱི་ངན་སོང་གི། སྡུག་བསྔལ་ངལ་སོའི་དགེ་བ: the genitive ཀུན་གྱི་ binds 'all sentient beings' to the lower-realm suffering. bo-gyaltsab 3-1 glosses འཁོར་བར་གནས་པའི་སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན་གྱི་ངན་སོང་གི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ངལ་གསོ་ཞིང་... འཐོབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་རྒྱུའི་དགེ་བ (virtue that gives all beings rest from their lower-realm suffering); bo-shenga likewise. The English makes the virtue 'of' the beings and leaves unstated whose suffering is relieved.
issues.fix:
In the virtue that gives all sentient beings rest
From the suffering of the lower realms

issues.span: Those afflictions subjected to suffering by natural death—
issues.evidence: Here ཉོན་མོངས་ is not the mental afflictions but a word of pity for the ordinary enemies of the battle simile. bo-kunpal 4-37: དགྲ་བོ་ཐ་མལ་པ་ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ཞེས་སྨད་པའི་ཚིག་སྟེ་ཉམས་ཐག་ཅིང་སྙིང་རྗེ་བའི་གནས་སུ་གྱུར་པའི་དགྲ་བོ་འདི་དག (ordinary enemies, 'wretched', objects of pity); bo-shenga 4-37: ཉོན་མོངས་ཏེ་སྙིང་རྗེའི་གནས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་དག. The mental afflictions are the target only of the application in the following verse. Rendering with the locked term 'afflictions' gives the wrong referent and collapses simile and application.
issues.fix: Those wretched enemies, made to suffer by their very nature as mortals who must die,

issues.span: One should speak of good qualities in their absence,
issues.evidence: ལྐོག་ན་ཡོན་ཏན་བརྗོད་བྱ: the qualities are those of others, praised behind their backs to avoid the suspicion of flattery. bo-gyaltsab 5-76: ཁ་གསག་ཏུ་དོགས་པས་ལྐོག་ན་གཞན་གྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ; bo-shenga 5-76 similar. 'Their' has no antecedent in the English.
issues.fix: One should speak of others' good qualities behind their backs,

issues.span: One should understand that as them knowing good qualities.
issues.evidence: ཡོན་ཏན་ཤེས་པར་རིག་པར་བྱ: the one to be recognized as knowing qualities is the speaker who praises one. bo-kunpal 5-76: བརྗོད་མཁན་པོ་དེ ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཁྱད་པར་ཤེས་པའི་མཁས་པ ... རིག་པར་བྱ་དགོས; bo-gyaltsab 5-76 adds that one should not become conceited. 'Them' is vague and the sense is hard to parse.
issues.fix: one should regard the speaker as someone who recognizes good qualities, and not become conceited.

issues.evidence: Tibetan གང་ཞིག་བསྒྲིམས་ཏེ་ཁྲོ་འཇོམས་པ states that the person (resolutely) destroys anger; Sanskrit 'yaḥ krodhaṃ hanti nirbandhāt'. Kunpal 6-6 glosses ཁྲོ་བའི་དགྲ་དེ་འཇོམས་པར་བྱེད་པའི་བཟོད་པ་བསྒོམ་པ. 'Strives to' turns an accomplished act into mere attempt and loses བསྒྲིམས་ཏེ ('firmly/determinedly').

issues.span: Whoever does not depend on anything
issues.evidence: Tibetan གང་ཞིག་ཀུན་ལ་ལྟོས་མེད་པ; Sanskrit 'nirāśaḥ yas tu sarvatra' (without hope/expectation). Kunpal 8-175 glosses ཀུན་ལ་རེ་འདོད་ཀྱིས་ལྟོས་པ་མེད་པ (no looking-to with hope or desire) for all desirable things; Shenga ལུས་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ཀུན་ལ་ལྟོས་པ་མེད་པར་གནས་པ. 'Depend on' suggests reliance/need, whereas the sense is having no expectation or craving.
issues.fix: Whoever has no expectation of anything

issues.evidence: Tibetan ནུས་མེད་འདོད་པ is 'desiring [what one] lacks the capacity [to achieve]'. Gyaltsab 8-175: འདོད་པ་རྫོགས་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ནུས་པ་མེད་བཞིན་དུ་འདོད་པ; Kunpal སྒྲུབ་པའི་ནུས་པ་མེད་བཞིན་དུ་འགྲུབ་པར་འདོད་པ. 'The impossible' is stronger than lack of ability.
issues.fix: From desiring what one lacks the ability to achieve

issues.span:
"If, because one endowed with other conditions sees,
it is luminous to itself,"
through the application of accomplished eye ointment,
the vase is seen, but not the eye ointment itself.
issues.evidence: Lines 1-2 are the opponent's (Cittamātrin) claim, lines 3-4 the reply (Shenga 9-24: 'འདིས་ཀྱང་ཤེས་པའི་རང་རིག་པ་གྲུབ་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བསྟན་པ'; Kunpal ཟེར་ན། དེར་མ་ངེས་ཏེ). The English runs the quoted objection straight into the reply with no break, and 'it' has no antecedent (the cognition/mind, Kunpal རང་སེམས).
issues.fix: "If one endowed with other conditions sees [others' minds], then [the mind] is luminous to itself." [Not so:] through applying accomplished eye ointment, one sees the vase, yet it does not become the eye ointment itself.

issues.span: through the power of the ones to be tamed and aspiration prayers
issues.evidence: Tibetan གདུལ་བྱ་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས. Kunpal 9-35 reads དེ་བཞིན་གདུལ་བྱར་... སྔོན་གྱི་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས་རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུར་སྣང་ངོ་ (to the disciples, through the power of earlier aspiration prayers, the Victor's body appears); Shenga: གདུལ་བྱར་སྔོན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་གནས་སྐབས་ན་བཏབ་པའི་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས་... རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུར་སྣང་ངོ་. The disciples are those to whom the form appears; the power is that of the (earlier) aspiration prayers. The English makes the disciples a causal power alongside the prayers and omits that the form appears to them.
issues.fix: Likewise, to those to be tamed, through the power of aspiration prayers [made earlier], the form of the Victor appears.
